# Weavers of the Void®: How the World Connects

A guide to the living parts of the world and the ways each one reaches into the others. Nothing in the world happens alone: a harvest feeds a city, the city raises an army, the army's war empties the granaries, and hunger turns hearts toward new gods. This booklet follows every one of those paths.

## How to read this booklet

- The world is divided into **parts**: the body, the mind, society, the economy, faith, war, the cosmos and more.
- Each part holds **mechanics**. A mechanic is one working of the world, described in a sentence: what happens, to whom, and why.
- Mechanics reach beyond their own part in four ways:
  - **Modifier**: one part raises or lowers a value that another part relies on, for as long as the cause lasts.
  - **Rule switch**: a world rule decides whether this connection works at all.
  - **Flow**: what one part produces, another part takes up.
  - **Trigger**: something that happens in one part sets something in motion in another.
- Every mechanic below lists the parts it reaches, the parts it draws on, what it acts upon, and the actions your sons and mortals can take on it.
- The world moves in **epochs** of fifty years. In each epoch every step runs once, in the order given at the end of this booklet.

<a id="m-events"></a>

#### Events: kinds, years and seasons, footprint, phases and the toll by cohort

- **Passes on to Demography:** famines, plagues and sieges kill by cohort at their height.
- **Bends Economy:** a plague's aftermath makes the survivors' labour dear.
- **Passes on to Environment:** famine and siege aftermaths leave sickness in the soil; massacres haunt the land.
- **Bends Society:** festivals and coronations calm unrest; riots vent it.
- **Bends Faith:** eclipse watches raise piety; schism councils split the faith.
- **Sets off events in Culture:** the chronicler marks every turn of a famine, plague or siege.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: event, region, settlement, people.

<a id="m-event_memory"></a>

#### Every multi-season event passes from onset to peak, aftermath and memory, and the communities it struck keep it

- **Passes on to Mind:** communities an event struck keep it as a memory.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: event, settlement, people.

<a id="m-storyteller_palette"></a>

#### Every subsystem registers its disruptions and recoveries; the storyteller weighs only those whose causes hold in each world

- **Bends Core:** subsystems that have not acted lately weigh more.
- **Bends Core:** a quiet world leans toward disruptions and a heated one toward recoveries.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: world.

<a id="m-foodways"></a>

#### Foodways

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world.

<a id="m-event_collections"></a>

#### Histories: incidents gathered into wars, battles, sieges, duels, plagues, gatherings and every other kind, nested and closed

- **Passes on to Core:** the chronicler tells the incidents of an age as parts of the histories they belong to.
- **Sets off events in Law:** many executions in one realm in one epoch make a purge.

Its effects reach Communication, Culture, Demography, Ecology, Economy, Faith, Household, Knowledge, Law, Mind, Society and War. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: mortal, people, settlement, polity, place, region.

<a id="m-modifiers"></a>

#### Modifier bus

- **Bends Body:** wounds and temperament weigh on a mortal's abilities.
- **Bends Law:** laws in force bend the communities under them.
- **Bends Culture:** traditions and renowned art lift the communities that keep them.
- **Bends Faith:** tenets and fanaticism move a faith's zeal and influence.
- **Bends Polity:** treaties in force steady or shake their parties.
- **Bends Economy:** temples, walls and houses of learning serve their community.
- **Bends Gods:** curses, blessings, divine gifts and dead gods bend what they touch.

Its effects reach Body, Culture, Economy, Faith, Gods, Law and Polity. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: mortal, people, settlement, cult, polity, region, place, army.

<a id="m-yearly_variance"></a>

#### Sampled years under one budget: births, fires, mine hazards, disease seasons and market swings

- **Passes on to Demography:** births and deaths are lived year by year in the epoch's sampled years.
- **Bends Demography:** a wet, hot sickly season in a sampled year speeds spread and deaths.
- **Bends Economy:** a sampled year's lost growth lifts food prices; other goods swing.
- **Sets off events in Environment:** the budget caps every sampled-year evaluation and counts what it extrapolates.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: people, settlement, region.

<a id="m-sub_clocks"></a>

#### Sampled years, campaign seasons and notable years

- **Passes on to War:** each war lives through campaign seasons with a real season, year and weather.
- **Passes on to Economy:** the epoch's harvest is the mean of its sampled years.
- **Passes on to Culture:** hungry years become famine records, remembered and fasted for.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: region, army.

<a id="m-settle_modes"></a>

#### Settle modes

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world.

<a id="m-storyteller_depth"></a>

#### Slow-burn and episodic storytellers, aims shaped by set points, and tension per region and per part of the world

- **Bends Core:** a region in crisis keeps a quiet world from being hurried.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: world.

<a id="m-society_kinds"></a>

#### Society kinds

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world.

<a id="m-storyteller"></a>

#### Storyteller: the tension of each world against its aim, the pace of spontaneous disruptions, recoveries, variety and the spotlight

- **Bends Ecology:** beasts appear more or less often.
- **Bends War:** feuds turn to raids more or less often, and peace comes sooner after hard years.
- **Bends Demography:** plagues strike more or less often; healers are born more often after hard years.
- **Bends Polity:** ambitious regents seize thrones more or less often.
- **Sets off events in Economy:** a heated world's hardest pressed community is given a full harvest.
- **Bends Society:** the spotlit record is chosen more often by agents and the chronicler.
- **Turns on or off in Culture:** a quiet world is revived only when the storyteller finds it quiet.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: world.

#### Time shares

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on Body, Communication, Cosmos, Culture, Demography, Ecology, Economy, Environment, Faith, Gods, Household, Intrigue, Knowledge, Language, Law, Mind, Polity, Society and War. It acts on: mortal, people.

Its effects reach Body, Communication, Cosmos, Culture, Demography, Ecology, Economy, Environment, Faith, Gods, Household, Knowledge, Law, Magic, Mind, Polity, Society and War. It draws on every other part of the world.

<a id="part-body"></a>

### Body

30 mechanics. Body reaches Economy, War, Environment, Polity, Society, Mind, Culture, Knowledge, Faith, Cosmos, Ecology, Gods, Law, Demography, Intrigue, Magic, Core, Communication, Household and Language.

<a id="m-possession_imprint"></a>

#### A possessing spirit lays its imprint over its host's values; the host's stress eats at its sanity until an exorcism rite drives the spirit out

- **Passes on to Mind:** the host's stress wears down its sanity.
- **Bends Magic:** an exorcism rite drives the spirit out.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: spirit, mortal, rite.

<a id="m-disease_agents"></a>

#### Agents of disease: what a disease is decides which cures work, where it survives and how fast it changes

- **Bends Faith:** a cure that fails costs a community's healers trust.
- **Sets off events in Knowledge:** healers of enough medicine learn what a disease is.
- **Sets off events in Ecology:** a reservoir kind or soil keeps a disease in its land.
- **Bends Body:** an overused cure breeds resistance.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: disease, people, settlement. Sons and mortals can act on it: answer sickness and seek cure.

<a id="m-augments"></a>

#### Augments lift skills and body functions, integrate or strain their bearers, cost upkeep and may be rejected

- **Passes on to Mind:** a straining augment stresses its bearer.
- **Bends Faith:** a faith that holds augments an abomination strains its faithful who bear them.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: mortal, beast, spirit. Sons and mortals can act on it: install augment and remove augment.

<a id="m-anatomy"></a>

#### Body plans

- **Passes on to Ecology:** a species' traits add wings, venom glands, horns and tails.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: mortal, species, son, foreign god.

<a id="m-body_systems"></a>

#### Body systems and sensitivities: what each body bears decides where its people can live and what it cannot meet

- **Bends Economy:** a world past what a people bears weighs on its towns.
- **Sets off events in Demography:** a colony is not founded where its settlers' bodies cannot bear the world.
- **Sets off events in Body:** a being meets what it is sensitive to and falls ill.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: people, species, mortal, settlement.

<a id="m-carriers"></a>

#### Carriers: named mortals carry a sickness unseen and seed it where they travel, until physicians who know contagion find them

- **Sets off events in Demography:** a carrier who travels seeds an outbreak where it goes.
- **Sets off events in Knowledge:** a physician who knows contagion finds a carrier.

Its effects reach Demography and Knowledge. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: mortal, disease. Sons and mortals can act on it: find carrier.

<a id="m-cognitive_decline"></a>

#### Cognitive decline: the old may lose their memory by degrees, forgetting skills, teaching less and losing office

- **Bends Knowledge:** a failing mind forgets what it learned and cannot teach.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: mortal.

<a id="m-agentless_conditions"></a>

#### Conditions without an agent: bodies that wear by age, diet, fouling, heredity, strain and old wounds, and ease by medicine

- **Bends Economy:** want in a town brings conditions of diet and their care costs wealth.
- **Bends Environment:** foul air, water and soil bring conditions of exposure.
- **Sets off events in Household:** a condition of a parent passes to the child.
- **Bends Knowledge:** a people's medicine eases its conditions.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: mortal, world. Sons and mortals can act on it: seek cure and ease body.

<a id="m-designed_disease"></a>

#### Diseases made by design strike whom they were aimed at, get loose among their makers and are answered by cultured cures

- **Bends Demography:** a designed disease kills more of those it was made for.
- **Sets off events in Body:** a designed disease may get loose among its makers.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: mortal, people, settlement. Sons and mortals can act on it: design disease and design cure.

<a id="m-genetics"></a>

#### Every mortal carries a genome of typed loci; children inherit one allele from each parent, the stronger shows, and kin unions raise harmful pairs

- **Bends Demography:** fertile or barren lines move the chance of children.
- **Bends Body:** long-lived, brief-lived and cursed lines lengthen or shorten a life.
- **Bends Body:** hardy or frail lines move the chance of catching a sickness.
- **Bends Mind:** a line prone to madness breaks a mind sooner under strain.
- **Bends Society:** beauty, read by the people's tastes in looks, feeds presence.
- **Sets off events in Polity:** a house is known by the look most of its line shares, and houses weigh kin matches by their ethics.
- **Passes on to Culture:** portraits keep the same face, drawn from the looks, scars and marks of afflictions.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: mortal, people, house. Sons and mortals can act on it: shape blood.

<a id="m-exposure"></a>

#### Exposure: cold, wet, hunger and fatigue gathered on the way, eased by healers and medicine, harming members past their limit

- **Passes on to Environment:** a cold land chills the party.
- **Sets off events in Body:** exposure past its limit harms.

<a id="m-keystone_resource"></a>

#### A world-defining resource: one producer's yield needed by an institution and held sacred, its harvest, monopoly, scarcity and wars

- **Passes on to Ecology:** harvesting the keystone thins its producers.
- **Passes on to Economy:** the controller of the source holds a monopoly.
- **Passes on to Faith:** the holding cult turns on a controller who lets it run short.
- **Sets off events in War:** the source is the main aim of war.
- **Passes on to Society:** those who depend on it suffer when it is scarce.
- **Sets off events in Cosmos:** a young world comes to depend on a rare sacred yield at once.
- **Passes on to Environment:** a keystone that no living species yields renews by itself.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: world, region, species, cult, polity. Sons and mortals can act on it: designate keystone.

<a id="part-polity"></a>

### Polity

63 mechanics. Polity reaches Economy, War, Environment, Society, Culture, Mind, Knowledge, Body, Faith, Cosmos, Ecology, Law, Gods, Intrigue, Demography, Communication, Magic, Core, Household and Language.

<a id="m-crises"></a>

#### A demand to cede land, release a vassal, convert or pay opens a crisis; backers weigh in until a side yields or it becomes war

- **Sets off events in War:** a war over a claim, a faith or a debt may open as a crisis instead.
- **Sets off events in Intrigue:** a demander owes a favour to swing parties who backed it.
- **Bends Polity:** the side that backs down loses legitimacy.
- **Sets off events in Faith:** a realm that concedes takes up the demander's faith.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: polity. Sons and mortals can act on it: issue demand and back crisis.

<a id="m-church_and_crown"></a>

#### A god-king's faith fuses the high priesthood with the crown; otherwise the clergy's sway drives investiture quarrels as typed incidents

- **Bends Polity:** the clergy's sway stirs quarrels with the crown.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: cult, polity, mortal.

<a id="m-court_scholar"></a>

- **Bends Knowledge:** the scholar's learning quickens research.
- **Passes on to Economy:** the stipend comes out of the treasury.
- **Passes on to Polity:** the ruler gains prestige as a patron.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: polity, mortal.

<a id="m-army_templates"></a>

- **Bends War:** a raised army fills its template's share before its doctrine.
- **Sets off events in Knowledge:** new arms outdate a template until the marshal refits it.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: polity.

<a id="m-court"></a>

- **Passes on to Society:** grandeur wins the ruler renown and draws skilled mortals to the capital.
- **Bends Polity:** grandeur warms other realms' trust.
- **Passes on to Body:** a court physician heals the ruler and a tutor sharpens the heir.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: polity, mortal. Sons and mortals can act on it: appoint court.

<a id="m-unjustified_war"></a>

#### A war without a ripe casus belli is unjustified: its ruler gains tyranny, other realms see a threat and its own people back it less

- **Passes on to Mind:** the ruler of an unjustified attacker gains tyranny.
- **Bends Polity:** every other realm sees a threat in it.
- **Bends Society:** its own people back the war less.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: polity.

- **Passes on to Society:** a realm's default may break its bank.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: polity, faction. Sons and mortals can act on it: rescue polity and repudiate debts.

- **Sets off events in Ecology:** an escaped line runs wild as a kind of its own.
- **Bends Economy:** a bred yield lifts what orchards give their owners.
- **Passes on to Faith:** a faith judges those who make life by its stance.
- **Sets off events in Law:** a realm bans, licenses or frees each way of living craft.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: mortal, beast, spirit, son, foreign god, creator, world, star, people, polity, cult, house, region, settlement. Sons and mortals can act on it: breed line, design line, bank sample, plant line, raise line, release line, license line, bless line and curse line.

<a id="m-living"></a>

#### Living made things eat, grow by stage, heal, age, breed, drift, bond with their handlers and die back into the land

- **Passes on to Economy:** a living thing eats from its town's stores each season.
- **Passes on to War:** a living army heals its wounded when fed and wears down when starved.
- **Passes on to Environment:** a dead living thing gives its fertility back to the land.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: mortal, beast, spirit, son, foreign god, creator, world, star, people, polity, cult, house, region, settlement. Sons and mortals can act on it: grow structure, grow vessel, grow gear and found living works.

<a id="m-eco_transformations"></a>

#### Long ecological transformation: plans remake a world's land a step each epoch against the pull of its climate and the folk who live from it

- **Passes on to Environment:** moisture, forest and soil move toward the plan's targets.
- **Bends Environment:** a harsh climate takes back part of each step.
- **Sets off events in Society:** folk who live from the old land sabotage the work.
- **Passes on to Environment:** a sabotage takes the land back a step.

Its effects reach Environment and Society. It draws on Environment, Faith, Household, Knowledge, Polity and Society. It acts on: region, world, polity, faction, settlement. Sons and mortals can act on it: sabotage remaking.

- **Passes on to Society:** a slain beast brings its hunter renown.
- **Sets off events in Culture:** a slain beast passes into a ballad its hunter's town sings.
- **Bends Knowledge:** study of the quarry makes the hunt likelier.

### Gods

37 mechanics. Gods reaches Economy, Environment, War, Polity, Society, Mind, Culture, Knowledge, Body, Faith, Cosmos, Ecology, Law, Demography, Intrigue, Magic, Core, Household, Communication and Language.

<a id="m-domain_economy"></a>

- **Passes on to War:** battles feed gods of war.

- **Passes on to Economy:** harvests feed gods of harvest.
- **Passes on to Cosmos:** madness feeds gods of madness.

<a id="m-divine_power_grammar"></a>

#### Divine powers built from a verb, an object, a scope, a mode, a cost, a cooldown, a strength and the domains they draw on

- **Bends Gods:** a power's strength grows with the domains its holder holds.
- **Sets off events in Society:** triggered powers act when the faithful are threatened or hungry.
- **Passes on to Economy:** powers over goods make or take stock.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: son, foreign god, mortal, people, settlement. Sons and mortals can act on it: wield power.

#### Divine servitors: beings in a god's service, each serving in one role, loyal while their god is regarded

- **Bends War:** the host adds to its god's might in divine battles.
- **Sets off events in Faith:** a disloyal servitor may fall to a rival or an outer being.
- **Sets off events in Faith:** the soul of a saint in a rewarding stratum may rise as a servitor of its god.
- **Bends War:** the host loses loyalty when its god is overcome in a divine battle.
- **Bends Gods:** each new command wears on a servitor's loyalty.

Its effects reach Communication, Faith and War. It draws on Body, Core, Cosmos, Culture, Demography, Ecology, Economy, Environment, Faith, Household, Knowledge, Magic, Mind, Polity, Society and War. <a id="m-dominion"></a>

#### Dominion and scales: each god's presence over every region, spreading from temples, holy sites, thrones, prophets, miracles and worship, contested, and leaning the land

- **Bends Environment:** the ruling god's scales move danger, fertility, heat and magic density in its regions.
- **Bends Economy:** order and productivity raise the prosperity and harvests of a dominated region.
- **Bends Demography:** growth and death move the population growth of a dominated region.
- **Bends Environment:** fortune and misfortune move the odds of disasters in a dominated region.
- **Bends Core:** turmoil in a dominated region raises the tension of its world.
- **Bends Faith:** missionaries convert more easily where their god rules the land.
- **Bends Magic:** miracles and rites cost less in one's own dominion and more in another god's.
- **Bends Mind:** worshippers feel their god near and priests of other gods feel out of place.
- **Passes on to Gods:** a son draws existence from the regions its dominion rules.
- **Sets off events in Gods:** a god's own deeds move its scales toward them.
- **Bends Law:** order raises public order and lowers crime in a dominated region, and turmoil stirs unrest.
- **Bends Economy:** productivity raises the output of mines, quarries, forests and works, and sloth lowers it.
- **Bends Body:** growth speeds the healing of wounds in a dominated region, and death slows it.
- **Bends Faith:** death stirs the spirits of a dominated region.
- **Bends Magic:** a god's rites work better where its dominion holds the land.
- **Bends Faith:** a god's miracles win more belief where its dominion holds the land.
- **Sets off events in Faith:** a disaster in a dominated region is blamed on its ruling god.
- **Passes on to Demography:** the more folk worship a god in a region, the more dominion they give it.

Its effects reach every other part of the world. It draws on every other part of the world. It acts on: son, foreign god, creator, region, world.

Every connection described in words, gathered by the two parts it joins.

### Within Core

- A quiet world leans toward disruptions and a heated one toward recoveries. *Modifier, from [Every subsystem registers its disruptions and recoveries; the storyteller weighs only those whose causes hold in each world](#m-storyteller_palette).*

- A covenant draws vis from its order's sites. *Flow, from [Magical orders: laws among mages, tribunals that judge breaches, and covenants that draw vis from held sites and teach magic to their town](#m-magical_orders).*

## Lasting influences

Some causes keep bending a value for as long as they last: a wound weakens, a blessing lifts, a law taxes. Each row names the cause, the value it bends and the mechanics that feel it.
